quote: I know now, I understand at last, Constantine, that for us, whether we write or act, it is not the honour and glory of which I have dreamt that is important, it is the strength to endure.
source: Anton Chekhov, The Sea-Gull, Act IV, her last speech to Treplieff (Nina) (trans. Marian Fell, 1912)
speaker: Nina

evidence.where: Archive.org OCR of the Cornell copy of Plays by Anton Tchekoff, translated by Marian Fell (Charles Scribner’s Sons; Copyright 1912, Published September 1912), page 220, running head THE SEA-GULL ACT IV; cross-checked with Project Gutenberg ebook 1754, which prints the same text without naming Fell
evidence.edition: Plays by Anton Tchekoff, trans. Marian Fell (New York: Charles Scribner’s Sons, 1912)
evidence.locator: The Sea-Gull, Act IV, p. 220, the sentence before One must know how to bear one’s cross, and one must have faith

reason: The sentence is verbatim in the scanned 1912 Scribner volume whose title page names Marian Fell, and in the Gutenberg transcription of it. Not shipped; Chekhov has one line in the year (January) and none in March.
